transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-03
Start: 3:00 PM PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Elena (Redwood CSM); Sarah (Trident CTO), Markus (Trident MLOps), Priya (Trident Platform), Jon (Trident Security), Alicia (Trident SRE)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): Quick onboarding kickoff: confirm goals for pilot, security/SSO and VPC needs, Dedicated vs hosted decision factors, ramp plan and next steps. Discussed timelines, success metrics, and initial pilot scope (search/QA assistant for clinician portal).

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can go ahead and get started. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Carlos our SE and Elena who will be your CSM.
[00:18] Sarah (Trident): Hi all, thanks. I'm Sarah, CTO at Trident. We have Markus, Priya, Jon and Alicia on the call. Excited to kick this off.
[00:30] Maya: Great. Quick agenda — align on pilot goals, confirm infra and security constraints, talk timeline, assign owners. We'll also cover onboarding steps and what we need to provision.
[00:45] Carlos (Redwood): Hi everyone, quick intro from me — I focus on performance and infra for inference. We'll likely recommend a small dedicated pool for the pilot but can start hosted depending on your data residency concerns.
[01:05] Markus (Trident): A couple of constraints up front — we are HIPAA scoped, data residency must remain in us-west-2 for the pilot, and we need audit logs + KMS integration. We also use Okta for SSO.
[01:25] Elena (Redwood): Thanks Markus. We do SOC2 and we have KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for Private deployments; we'll share the security pack.
[01:40] Jon (Trident): Important: we need details on network — VPC peering or private link? Also, can you support air-gapped on-prem later?
[01:55] Carlos: Yes. We support VPC peering and private endpoints; on-prem package is possible though more involved. For the pilot, peering into your VPC in us-west-2 is typical. We'll share a network checklist.
[02:10] Priya: Timeline question — we want the pilot running in about 4 weeks. Is that realistic?
[02:22] Maya: 4 weeks is doable for a data-plane hosted or dedicated quick pilot. If you require an on-prem install or strict air-gap, that will add time.
[02:35] Alicia (Trident): Cost is a concern — we want predictable spend. How does Redwood approach cost controls, burst vs reserved?
[02:48] Carlos: We have Dedicated with reserved capacity (monthly commits) and autoscale/burst. For pilots many customers use a small dedicated pool to measure throughput and then adjust. We also have batching/cache settings to optimize token cost — e.g., KV cache and prefix caching to reduce per-token cost.
[03:10] Sarah: Can you explain KV cash? sorry, I mean KV cache — we've seen notes in the docs.
[03:17] Carlos: Yeah KV cache — sorry transcription — that's the key value op-cache for previous context; helps when you have repeated prefixes like patient prompts. It reduces repeated compute.
[03:35] Markus: From infra side we need to understand latency SLOs. We have clinician-facing features that need sub-300ms for short prompts. Can you hit that in us-west-2?
[03:52] Carlos: For small models and tuned kernels, yes for generation under X tokens. For larger models, we'd recommend model variants or quantized variants. We can run a perf bench during pilot.
[04:08] Maya: We'll add a benchmark step to the pilot scope — measure p50/p90 latency and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:20] Sarah: Ok good. Security — we need SAML/Okta integration and enterprise RBAC plus audit logs for clinician access.
[04:33] Elena: We support SAML/Okta and SCIM for provisioning and detailed audit logs. We'll send the SSO integration doc and RBAC mapping example.
[04:48] Jon: On encryption — KMS for data at rest and also key management for logs?
[04:56] Carlos: We integrate with AWS KMS and can work with customer-managed CMKs. Logs can be routed to your logging stack; we can redact PII on ingestion if needed.
[05:12] Maya: Quick note on models — do you plan to use Red models from our catalog or bring your own?
[05:20] Priya: We were planning to test one of the open LLMs you've listed but may want to try a fine-tuned model later.
[05:28] Carlos: Fine. We can serve open models and also support model artifacts if you want to bring them; for POC usually start with open model verified by Redwood with quantization.
[05:42] Markus: Ok walkthrough of onboarding steps?
[05:48] Elena: We'll do three phases: 1) Setup & access — SSO, VPC peering, KMS, accounts. 2) Pilot deployment — provision small dedicated cluster or hosted route, deploy model, run workloads. 3) Evaluation & rollouts — benchmarks, quality checks, roll to prod or scale.
[06:05] Maya: For success criteria — what metrics do you care about? Latency, cost, and correctness (F1/QA pass rates)?
[06:16] Sarah: Exactly — latency (<300ms p90), cost per 1k tokens target (TBD), and quality measured on our prompt set passing >85% accuracy for the clinician assistant.
[06:32] Maya: Perfect — we'll draft a success criteria doc for the pilot.
[06:36] 
[06:40] [Slide share note: Maya shared onboarding deck link: https://redwood.infra/docs/onboarding-deck (note: link placeholder)]

[07:00] Carlos: On the technical deep dive items we'll cover later: model quantization profiles, kernel selection, batching strategy, autoscale policies and failover routing. Any initial questions?
[07:18] Priya: A question about private deployments: after pilot, if we want customer-managed control plane, does Redwood support that?
[07:27] Maya: Yes, Redwood Private offers customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem package. That would change timeline and costs; we'll include those options in the deck.
[07:40] Jon: About compliance: do you have penetration test reports and SOC2 type 2 cert?
[07:47] Elena: Yes we have SOC2 Type II. We'll share the summary report and penetration testing artifacts under NDA.
[07:59] Markus: Great. For the bench — can you run perf tests against our representative prompt set and traffic shape?
[08:08] Carlos: Yes, we'll need a sample prompt set and expected RPS. We'll also instrument tracing for latency breakdowns.
[08:18] Alicia: For networking, we prefer VPC peering and direct routing. Any gotchas we should expect?
[08:26] Carlos: We'll share a network checklist; common gotchas are route tables, security group egress for the worker nodes, and MTU settings. Also certs for private endpoints.
[08:40] Sarah: Stakeholders — we'll loop in procurement and legal after the pilot.
[08:47] Maya: Noted. We'll also put together an initial price estimate for the pilot size and expected spikes.

[09:05] [Timestamp jump — later in call, deeper technical Q&A]
[09:10] Markus: Regarding model variants — how does the runtime handle fallbacks if the dedicated pool is saturated?
[09:18] Carlos: We have smart routing — requests can failover to hosted or cheaper variants; there is a policy layer to prefer latency or cost. You can set automatic fallback to quantized or smaller models.
[09:32] Priya: How are rolling upgrades handled? We can't have heavy downtime.
[09:37] Carlos: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallbacks. The console shows per-route metrics so you can validate before shifting traffic.
[09:48] Jon: Is there a way to redact PHI before sending to Redwood if needed?
[09:54] Elena: We offer client-side redaction examples and also server-side ingestion filters. We'll add a sample pipeline.

[10:12] Maya: Ok let's capture decisions: pilot scope: clinician assistant in portal, start with hosted model or small Dedicated in us-west-2, SSO via Okta, VPC peering, KMS CMK, benchmark for latency and cost.
[10:28] Sarah: Agree.

[10:35] Maya: Next steps and owners — Elena will send security pack, Carlos will schedule architecture deep dive, Maya will send deck and pricing. Markus to share infra diagram.
[10:46] Markus: I'll get that by end of week.
[10:50] Elena: I'll send SOC2 and SSO doc tomorrow.
[10:54] Maya: Great. Questions?
[11:00] Alicia: One last Q — do you have a staging flow for test data that keeps PHI isolated?
[11:08] Carlos: Yes we recommend a synthetic dataset for bench and provide hooks for redaction; we'll include examples.

[11:20] [Wrap up]
[11:22] Maya: Thanks everyone — we will recap in an email with next steps.
[11:26] Sarah: Thanks all.
[11:30] End of recording.
